title: Visual Hierarchy
summary: Hierarchy makes the next useful action and relationships among content levels perceptible through combined cues.

MUST.text: Combine at least two cues (size, weight, color, position, whitespace) for each level; do not rely on size alone.
Provide one dominant page heading and one primary action per view; subordinate supporting content.

SHOULD.text: Make the primary task identifiable within a quick scan of the screen.
Use a documented type/weight/space scale so levels stay consistent across screens.

AVOID.text: If two elements compete, reduce one or restructure the task.
Do not encode hierarchy through color alone (see VIS-003, A11Y-002).

DECIDE.decision: Largest/boldest in its region, isolated by whitespace
Preserve level order; stack, do not flatten
Reduce one or split the task

EXAMPLE.good: "Dashboard: KPI value 32px/bold, label 14px, comparison 12px muted, note 12px."
EXAMPLE.bad: "All dashboard text 16px with only color differences."

FAILURE_MODES: Equal visual weight causes users to miss the primary action.
Color-only hierarchy fails for color-blind and low-vision users.
Responsive reflow can flatten levels and hide priority.
Decorative elements compete with task content.

checks.text: At least two cues per level?
